Each page read for this pack instead names github.com/microsoftgraph/microsoft-graph-docs (the live/ branch, not -contrib) as its source, and that specific repository returns 404 to both the GitHub web UI and API as read here, so its own licence could not be confirmed directly; CC BY 4.0 is inferred from the public sibling repo, not read on the cited repo itself. Separately, the rendered learn.microsoft.com pages are also covered by https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/legal/termsofuse (read 2026-09-19), which limits Documents to informational, non-commercial or personal use and prohibits redistribution without Microsoft's written consent; that page states no CC grant. Entries here paraphrase the property tables (own words, quotes at or under twenty words, attributed by cite), which is compatible with either reading, but redistributing this pack's text at any larger scale should treat the Terms of Use limitation as live, not superseded by the CC BY 4.0 repo licence.

odata_type.format: A string naming a microsoft.graph.security resource type, for example #microsoft.graph.security.hostPair.

#microsoft.graph.security.host_idPair.meaning: A host pair, redirect or similar link (ms:defender:ti:hostpairs). The observed literal, not the vendor page's own hostPair spelling; kept as read, not corrected.

#microsoft.graph.security.hostCookie.meaning: A cookie name observed on a host (ms:defender:ti:cookies).

#microsoft.graph.security.articleIndicat.meaning: An indicator reported inside an article (ms:defender:ti:article_indicators).

artifact_type.format: A string naming the related artifact's resource type.

examples.note: passivedns; the DNS answer is an IP
article_indicators; the observed literal is lower-case hostname, not the vendor's hostName

domain_status.format: A comma-separated list of EPP/ICANN domain status codes, one string.

examples.value: client update prohibited,client transfer prohibited,client delete prohibited
examples.note: the one sample read here; codes are free text from the registry, not a fixed set documented by this API

dns_record_type.format: A DNS resource record type name.

examples.note: the only value the one sample read here shows; the vendor page does not enumerate the full set (AAAA, CNAME, MX, NS, TXT and others are the DNS standard, not confirmed against this API)

link_kind.format: A short word or phrase naming why two hosts are paired.
link_kind.quote: An example of this may be redirect.

finalRedirect.meaning: The parent host's final HTTP redirect lands on the child host.

component_category.format: A short category name for the detected component.
component_category.quote: for example, Operating System, Framework, Remote Access, or Server

Server.meaning: Server software, for example a web server.

indicator_source.format: One fixed word naming where the indicator originated.
indicator_source.quote: The possible values are: microsoft, osint, public, unknownFutureValue.

osint.meaning: Open-source threat intelligence reported the indicator.

public.meaning: A public source reported the indicator.

unknownFutureValue.meaning: A reserved placeholder for a value added after this API version; treat as unknown, not as one of the other three.

content_format.format: One fixed word naming the markup an article's body or summary content is written in.
content_format.quote: The possible values are: text, html, markdown, unknownFutureValue.

unknownFutureValue.meaning: A reserved placeholder for a value added after this API version.

examples.note: the one sample read here, for both body.format and summary.format

host_artifact_type.format: A string naming which host implementation this is.

examples.note: the one sample read here; abstract host has hostname and ipAddress implementations

cert_fingerprint.format: Lower-case hex, colon-delimited between byte pairs.

examples.note: the one sample read here; the same digest as sslCertificate.sha1 below, without colons
the one sample read here; the same digest as sslCertificate.fingerprint above, colon-delimited there

x500_address_type.format: A short word tagging the kind of address.

examples.note: the only value the one sample read here shows, on both issuer and subject

x500_common_name.format: Free text; a hostname when it names the certificate subject, an issuing CA's name when it names the issuer.

examples.note: subject.commonName in the one sample read here

splunk_host_id.format: A domain name or IP address string, whichever identifier the TA's input was configured with.

examples.note: the identifier most of the vendor's own worked examples use

cookie_domain.format: Free text; a hostname in the one sample read here, though the vendor's own description calls it a URI.
cookie_domain.quote: The URI for which the cookie is valid.

examples.note: the one sample read here; equal to host.id in that same record, which need not always hold

article_tags.format: A collection of short free-text tags; multivalue in Splunk.

examples.value: OSINT, Batloader, RoyalRansomware, Python, JavaScript, MSI, PowerShell
examples.note: the full tag list of the one sample read here, shown comma-joined

record_id.format: Base64-encoded composite key on seven containers; on subdomains the vendor example shows a plain GUID instead. Articles uses a separate concept, article_id.

article_id.format: A short opaque string, not base64 and not a GUID.

examples.note: the one sample read here; also the value article_indicators.splunk.articleId carries for its indicators
